title: Multicenter Randomized Phase II Proof-of-Concept Trial Evaluating the Effect of Semaglutide Plus Lifestyle Intervention on Biomarkers Potentially Associated with Lung Cancer Risk in Overweight or Obese Patients with Cardiovascular Disease and a History of Smoking (INTERCEPT-LUNG)
official: Multicenter Randomized Phase II Proof-of-Concept Trial Evaluating the Effect of Semaglutide Plus Lifestyle Intervention on Biomarkers Potentially Associated with Lung Cancer Risk in Overweight or Obese Patients with Cardiovascular Disease and a History of Smoking (INTERCEPT-LUNG)
summary: Main objective: To assess whether semaglutide + lifestyle intervention reduces hsCRP at 48 weeks in individuals with CVD and smoking history
conditions: A short-course preventive treatment with semaglutide, along with a lifestyle intervention in overweight/obese individuals at high risk of LC would significantly reduce levels of biomarkers linked to a high risk of lung cancer.

interventions.name: Wegovy 0.25 mg solution for injection in pre-filled pen
Wegovy 1.7 mg solution for injection in pre-filled pen
Wegovy 1 mg solution for injection in pre-filled pen
Wegovy 2.4 mg solution for injection in pre-filled pen

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Provides written informed consent for the trial
2. Males or females with ALL the following criteria: •	Age [50-74] •	No personal history of lung cancer, no suspicious lung lesion currently undergoing evaluation or follow-up; no symptoms suspicious for LC. Must have undergone LC screening with low-dose CT of chest in the past 3 months prior to inclusion in the study with a negative or indeterminate result as per the guidelines of the Société d’imagerie thoracique (60)   •	History of smoking (active or quit ≤ 15 years ago; ≥ 20 cigarettes/day for ≥ 20 years or ≥15 cigarettes/day for ≥ 25 years or ≥10 cigarettes/day for ≥ 30 years) •	Established atheromatous CVD which has been stable during the past 7 months (no major event) and as evidenced by at least one of the following:  a.	Coronary artery disease: Prior Myocardial infarction or prior revascularization (percutaneous coronary intervention or coronary artery bypass grafting) or medically managed symptomatic chronic coronary syndrome  b.	Prior stroke (non-cardioembolic ischemic stroke) and/or significant carotid artery stenosis (≥ 50% as per NASCET criteria) c.	Peripheral arterial disease (PAD): Presence of symptoms such as intermittent claudication (Fontaine ≥ II) or ankle-brachial index (ABI) ≤ 0.9 (at rest), or prior peripheral arterial revascularization procedure, or amputation due to atherosclerotic disease •	Have a body mass index (BMI) ≥ 27 kg/m2
3. A female participant is eligible to participate if she is not pregnant, not breastfeeding, and at least one of the following conditions applies: •	Not a woman of childbearing potential (WOCBP) OR •	A WOCBP. WOCBP must have a negative urine β-HCG pregnancy test within 7 days prior to registration. If the urine test is positive or cannot be confirmed as negative, a serum pregnancy test will be required. Sexually active female patients must agree to use two methods of effective contraception (cf. paragraph 6.12, one of them being a barrier method.
4. Participants must be in good general health in the opinion of the investigator based on the screening physical assessment
5. Adequate blood counts, liver and renal functions collected within 28 days prior to the start of study treatment: • Absolute neutrophil count (ANC) >= 1500/ul, Platelets >= 100 000/uL, Hemoglobin >= 9.0 g/dL or >= 5.6 mmol/L. Criteria must be met without erythropoietin dependency and without packed red blood cell (pRBC) transfusion within the last 90 days • Creatinine =< 1.5 x upper limit or normal (ULN) OR measured or calculated creatinine clearance (glomerular filtration rate (GFR) can also be used in place of creatinine or creatinine clearance [CrCl]) >= 30 mL/min for participant with creatinine levels > 1.5 x institutional ULN • Total bilirubin =< 1.5 x ULN OR direct bilirubin =< ULN for participants with total bilirubin levels > 1.5 x ULN; Aspartate aminotransferase (AST) (serum glutamic oxaloacetic transaminase [SGOT]) and alanine aminotransferase (ALT) (serum glutamic pyruvic transaminase [SGPT]) =< 2.5 x ULN
6. Patients must be affiliated to a social security system or beneficiary of the same.
Exclusion criteria:
1. Personal history of lung cancer, and of any other invasive cancer within the past 5 years or not in complete remission at the time of study entry. Note: Participants with basal cell carcinoma of the skin, squamous cell carcinoma of the skin or carcinoma in situ (e.g. breast or cervix) that have undergone treatment with curative intent are allowed to participate
2. Active tuberculosis
3. Participation in another clinical study with an investigational product during the last 28 days and while on study treatment
4. Positive (suspicious for cancer) baseline LDCT screening results
5. Long QT syndrome, family history of idiopathic sudden death or congenital long QT syndrome, or any of the following: Risk factors for Torsades de Pointe (TdP) including uncorrected hypokalemia or hypomagnesemia, , or history of clinically significant/symptomatic bradycardia Medication(s) with a known risk to prolong the QT interval and/or known to cause Torsades de Pointe that cannot be discontinued or replaced by safe alternative medication
6. Patients under guardianship or deprived of their liberty by a judicial or administrative decision or incapable of giving their consent.
7. Has known psychiatric or substance abuse disorders that would interfere with cooperation with the requirements of the trial
8. Psychological, familial, sociological or geographical conditions that do not permit compliance with the study protocol
9. Any disorder, unwillingness, or inability, which in the investigator’s opinion, might jeopardize the patient’s safety or compliance with the protocol
10. Personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or patients with Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia syndrome type 2
11. Known hypersensitivity to semaglutide or any of the product components
12. Patients with prior allogeneic stem cell or solid organ transplantation
13. History or presence of chronic pancreatitis
14. History of acute pancreatitis (at any time)
15. Treatment with a GLP-1RA within 90 days before the registration in the study
16. History of unstable cardiovascular disease within the past 7 months (major event such as acute coronary syndrome)
17. Have a known clinically significant gastric emptying abnormality (for example, diabetic gastroparesis or gastric outlet obstruction) or chronically take drugs that directly affect GI motility
18. Have taken within 3 months prior to inclusion, medications (prescribed or over-thecounter) or alternative remedies intended to promote weight loss. Examples include, but are not limited to Saxenda® (liraglutide 3.0 mg), Mounjaro® (tirzepatide), Xenical®/Alli® (orlistat), Meridia® (sibutramine), Acutrim® (phenylpropanolamine), Sanorex® (mazindol), Adipex® (phentermine), BELVIQ® (lorcaserin), Qsymia® (phentermine/topiramate combination), Contrave® (naltrexone/bupropion) Note: Use of metformin or any other glucose-lowering medication apart from GLP-1 and GIP-receptor agonist is permitted.
19. Have any hematological condition that may interfere with HbA1c measurement (for example, hemolytic anemias, sickle cell disease)
20. Have congestive heart failure New York Heart Association (NYHA) class IV.
21. Have active or unstable diabetic retinopathy judged by the investigator to be at high risk for progression with rapid glycemic improvement. Participants with non-proliferative or stable treated diabetic retinopathy may be enrolled. These participants must have had a documented ophthalmologic examination within the previous 12 months and will be advised to continue routine retinal surveillance during the study.
22. Severe cardiac or respiratory insufficiency (resting dyspnea) or other comorbidities that render the individual ineligible for lung cancer screening
23. Active or history of autoimmune disease or immune deficiency, including Type 1 diabetes mellitus on insulin regimen except for history of treated autoimmune-related hypothyroidism
24. Is pregnant or breastfeeding or expecting to conceive children within the projected duration of the study, starting with the screening visit until 2 months after the last dose of trial treatment
25. A WOCBP who has a positive urine pregnancy test within 72 hours prior to treatment. Note: if 72 hours have elapsed between the screening pregnancy test and the first dose of study treatment, another urine pregnancy test must be performed and must be negative to start receiving study medication
26. Current/previous treatments: • Systemic antineoplastic therapy including chemotherapy, immunotherapy and targeted therapy, biologic therapy and investigational agents within the past 5 years. Adjuvant hormonal therapy for breast cancer is allowed. • Treatment with systemic immunostimulatory agents (including but not limited to interferons or interleukin−2) within 4 weeks or five half-lives of the drug, whichever is shorter, prior to enrolment • Current treatment with anti-viral therapy for HBV infection • Treatment with a systemic immunosuppressive medication (including, but not limited to corticosteroids, cyclophosphamide, azathioprine, methotrexate and thalidomide) within 2 weeks prior to initiation of study treatment, or anticipation of need for systemic immunosuppressive medication during study treatment, with the following exceptions: - Patients who received acute, low-dose systemic immunosuppressant medication, or systemic corticosteroids at physiologic doses not to exceed <<10 mg/day>> of prednisone or its equivalent, or a one-time pulse dose of systemic immunosuppressant medication (e.g., 48 hours of corticosteroids as premedication for hypersensitivity reaction (e.g., CT scan premedication)) are eligible for the study - Patients who received mineralocorticoids (e.g., fludrocortisone), corticosteroids for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) or asthma, or low-dose corticosteroids for orthostatic hypotension or adrenal insufficiency are eligible for the study. Patients who received intranasal, inhaled, topical or local steroid injections (e.g., intra articular injection) are also eligible
27. Has received live vaccines within 30 days prior to first dose of study treatment and while participating in the study. Examples of live vaccines include but are not limited to: measles, mumps, rubella, varicella/zoster, yellow fever, rabies, Bacillus Calmette-Guerin (BCG) and typhoid vaccine. (Note: Seasonal influenza vaccines for injection are generally killed virus vaccines and are allowed; however intranasal influenza vaccines (eg FluMist) are live attenuated vaccines and are not allowed)
28. Known hypersensitivity to the planned therapies or any of their components
29. Patients with non-arteritic anterior ischaemic optic neuropathy (NAION) or suspected NAION.
30. History of intestinal occlusion
31. History of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, organizing pneumonia or interstitial lung disease
32. Has received a blood transfusion (e.g. platelets or plasma) within 90 days prior to study
33. Serious uncontrolled concomitant disease that would put the patient at high risk of treatment-related complications
34. Has an active infection requiring systemic therapy
35. History of HIV infection
36. Patients with active hepatitis infection (defined as having a positive hepatitis B surface antigen [HBsAg] test at screening) or hepatitis C. Patients with past hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection or resolved HBV infection (defined as having a negative HBsAg test and a positive to hepatitis B core antigen [anti-HBc] antibody test) are eligible. Patients positive for hepatitis C virus (HCV) antibody are eligible only if polymerase chain reaction (PCR) is negative for HCV RNA
